I farm in Singida where the rains are not always reliable, so I grow drought-tolerant crops like sorghum and groundnuts on this plot. Chemical fertilizer is too expensive and risky if the rains fail, but I will spread cow manure from my animals before planting to keep the soil fertile. I save my own seed each year because it works well here and costs nothing. We work the land with hand hoes—my family will spend many days planting, weeding twice, scaring birds, and harvesting, and during the busy weeding and harvest times I will hire a few workers to help so we finish on time.
